blocks.x: In over three years at Collider, senior author Jake has now penned over 3000 articles covering a wide range of TV and film for the resources, lists, utilities, news, and interview teams. Alongside interviewing stars such as Selin Hizli, Rose Ayling-Ellis, Harlan Coben, and Chelsea Peretti, Jake was lucky enough to visit the set of Aardman and Netflix's Wallace and Gromit: A Vengeance Most Fowl in 2024, getting the chance to chat with four-time Academy Award winner Nick Park and Merlin Crossingham. Jake has also worked for other publications, including Agents of Fandom. You can also hear Jake every week as the resident film and TV journalist on Track Radio.

After the disappointing commercial and critical performance of their last original idea, Elio, 2026 proved the perfect comeback for Pixar as they released Hoppers, a fresh family-friendly tale starring newcomer Piper Curda as an animal lover who uses technology to become a robotic beaver. Hoppers started the year off strong for Pixar, earning $388 million worldwide against a reported $150 million budget, and was called one of Pixar's "funniest movies yet" in Ross Bonaime's review for Collider.

But that was merely the appetizer for what would prove a fruitful main course for Pixar fans in 2026. Thanks to Woody (Tom Hanks), Buzz (Tim Allen), Jessie (Joan Cusack), and the rest of the Toy Story 5 gang, Pixar landed itself another billion-dollar hit. Following in the footsteps of the Chinese animated hit Ne Zha 2, the hilarious Zootopia 2, and the video game adaptation, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Toy Story 5 became the latest animated sequel to smash the billion-dollar boundary, and did so alongside glowing reviews suggesting the franchise was back on track after an underwhelming fourth installment.

"The impressive fifth installment not only justifies its existence but feels like a necessary response to how much the world has changed in the past three decades," wrote Collider's Taylor Gates in her 8/10 review of the movie, which was one of many that praised this return to form for Pixar's flagship franchise. But there was little chance this fifth film could ever reach the heights of Toy Story's peak, which came back in 1999 with what many consider to be the greatest animated sequel of all time: Toy Story 2.

Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes
Which Superhero Team Should You Join?
Avengers · X-Men · Teen Titans · The Boys

Every team is a personality test with a uniform. One saves the world and argues about it the whole way home. One has been fighting for the right to exist since the day it formed. One is still working out who it is while the fighting happens. And one has no powers at all, plus no intention of playing fair. Eight questions decide where you actually belong.

What kind of power would you actually want?
The power matters less than what you would be willing to do with it.

ASomething enormous and obvious. I would not hide it.
BSomething I was born with, whether I wanted it or not.
CSomething still growing that I cannot quite control.
DNone at all. I would rather nobody sees me coming.

Why join a team at all?
Nobody puts on the suit for the reason they say out loud.

ABecause some threats are too big for anyone alone.
BBecause people like me are safer together than apart.
CBecause I did not want to do any of this alone.
DBecause somebody has to hold these people accountable.

How do you feel about the people in charge?
Every team has a chain of command. Very few of them survive contact.

AI will follow a good leader and argue with a bad one.
BThey have never protected people like me. I expect nothing.
CI am still learning who to trust, and getting it wrong.
DThey are the problem. That is the entire point.

What is your role inside a group?
Every roster needs the same handful of people to function.

AThe big personality. I take up room and I earn it.
BThe one who protects whoever arrived most recently.
CThe heart. I keep everybody talking to each other.
DThe one who says the uncomfortable thing out loud.

How do you win a fight you should lose?
This is the scene the entire film gets built around.

AOverwhelming force, and a very good landing.
BWorking together in a way nobody saw coming.
CRefusing to give up long after I should have.
DPreparation, leverage, and one extremely dirty trick.

What is this work costing you?
Nobody does this for free. The bill just arrives differently for everyone.

AMy private life. Everybody knows my face now.
BMy safety. The world is frightened of me.
CMy childhood. I grew up faster than I should have.
DMy peace. I cannot stop now that I know.

How should the world see your team?
Half of this job is public relations, and everybody knows it.

AAs icons. The team everyone is relieved to see arrive.
BAs people. Just people, which is all we ever asked.
CAs proof the next generation is going to be fine.
DThey should not see us at all until it is done.

The offer arrives. What makes you say yes?
Eight questions in, this is the one that decides your team.

AThe scale. If the world is ending, I want to be there.
BThe promise that I would not have to hide anymore.
CThe people. I would be joining friends, not an employer.
DThe chance to take down somebody who deserves it.

Recruitment Is Complete
Your Team Is…

Four teams, four completely different reasons to put yourself in danger
for strangers. This is the roster you actually belong on, what they would want from you, and what it
would cost you to stay.

You belong where the stakes are largest and the personalities are
loudest. This is a team of people who are all used to being the most important person in the
room, which is exactly why it works and exactly why it keeps nearly falling apart.

The Avengers are not friends who became a team. They are a team that slowly and
reluctantly became friends, and you would recognise every stage of that process.

You can hold your own among big egos without needing to win every exchange, which is the
real entry requirement here.

The arguing is part of the method. This group does its best thinking mid-disagreement,
usually at volume, usually in a very expensive building.
When the sky opens, they are who shows up. You would want to be standing in that line.

You have never had the luxury of being thanked for this. The
X-Men protect a world that has never once been comfortable with them existing, and something
in you understands exactly why they keep doing it anyway.

This is the only team on the list whose central conflict is not a villain. It is being
wanted gone by the same people they keep saving.

You know what it is to be the outsider in a room and to decide, anyway, that you will
not make yourself smaller so everyone else is comfortable.

The X-Men are the most genuine found family in comics. People arrive with nowhere else
to go and are never once asked to explain themselves.
You would not be joining for the glory. There has never been any.

You do not want colleagues, you want your people. The Titans are
the team where the friendship came first and the world-saving turned up afterwards as an
inconvenient side effect.

Every Titan is somebody's sidekick who decided to stop being one. That decision, not the
villain of the week, is what the team is actually about.

You would be joining people who are all working themselves out at the same time as you,
which is far less lonely than being the only one.

The Titans lose regularly. Then they eat together and come back better, which is a more
honest model of growing up than any other team here manages.
The tower would be loud, chaotic, and the first place that ever felt like yours.

You are not asking who to trust. You worked out the answer a
while ago and it was nobody in a cape. This is where you go once you have decided the people
in charge need watching, and that nobody else is going to do it.

The Boys have no powers, no mandate and no funding. What they have is leverage,
patience, and a very high tolerance for consequences.

You are the person in the room who notices the thing everybody else has quietly agreed
not to mention.

This is not a heroic team and it has never pretended otherwise. It is a group of damaged
people doing necessary work in ways nobody would call clean.
You would not sleep well. You would keep going anyway.
